note: Reads 4-byte parser options from fuzzer input. Must include XML_PARSE_DTDVALID and XML_PARSE_NODICT to trigger the use-after-free.
XML_PARSE_HUGE is cleared to avoid timeouts. XML_PARSE_DTDVALID (0x80) and XML_PARSE_NODICT (0x40) remain set.
Reads URL/entity string pairs from fuzzer input. First entity is the main XML document.
Gets the main XML document buffer from the fuzzer input.

code: doc = xmlReadMemory(docBuffer, docSize, NULL, NULL, opts);
note: First parses with the pull parser. This validates the document and populates the refs table with IDREF attributes.
Serializes the document. This may reuse/free attribute structures.
Frees the pull-parsed document. With XML_PARSE_NODICT, attribute strings are not interned in a dictionary.
Creates a push parser context for the second parse of the same document.
Applies the same options including XML_PARSE_DTDVALID and XML_PARSE_NODICT to the push parser.

code: for (consumed = 0; consumed < docSize; consumed += chunkSize) { chunkSize = docSize - consumed; if (chunkSize > maxChunkSize) chunkSize = maxChunkSize; xmlParseChunk(ctxt, docBuffer + consumed, chunkSize, 0); }
note: Feeds the document to the push parser in chunks of at most 128 bytes. The parser validates and populates the refs table.
Terminates the push parser. This triggers xmlSAX2EndDocument which calls xmlValidateDocumentFinal, walking the refs table.
Frees the push-parsed document.
Frees the push parser context.

code: reader = xmlReaderForMemory(docBuffer, docSize, NULL, NULL, opts);
note: Creates a validating XML reader with XML_PARSE_DTDVALID and XML_PARSE_NODICT. This is the vulnerable code path.
Reads nodes one by one. When moving past a node, the reader frees the previous node's attributes via xmlTextReaderFreeProp.

code: xmlNodePtr tmp = reader->node->prev; if ((tmp->extra & NODE_IS_PRESERVED) == 0) { xmlUnlinkNode(tmp); xmlTextReaderFreeNode(reader, tmp); }
note: When the reader moves to the next sibling, it frees the previous node. This calls xmlTextReaderFreeNode which frees the node's properties.
Frees all properties (attributes) of the element node being discarded.
VULNERABLE: Only removes IDs from the doc->ids table. Does NOT remove IDREF attributes from the doc->refs table. The refs table still holds a pointer to this attribute.

code: if ((reader != NULL) && (reader->ctxt != NULL) && (reader->ctxt->freeAttrsNr < 100)) { cur->next = reader->ctxt->freeAttrs; reader->ctxt->freeAttrs = cur; reader->ctxt->freeAttrsNr++; } else { xmlFree(cur); }
note: The attribute is freed or placed on the free list. With XML_PARSE_NODICT, the attribute's name and children strings are not dictionary-interned, so the memory is actually freed.

code: if (xmlTextReaderNodeType(reader) == XML_ELEMENT_NODE) { int i, n = xmlTextReaderAttributeCount(reader); for (i=0; i<n; i++) { xmlTextReaderMoveToAttributeNo(reader, i); while (xmlTextReaderReadAttributeValue(reader) == 1); } }
note: The fuzzer reads all attributes of each element. This may increment preserves, but the key trigger is the freeing of IDREF attributes when nodes are discarded.
Continues reading until the end of the document. By the time the reader reaches the end, IDREF attributes from earlier nodes have been freed.

code: if (ctxt->validate && ctxt->wellFormed && ctxt->myDoc && ctxt->myDoc->intSubset) ctxt->valid &= xmlValidateDocumentFinal(&ctxt->vctxt, ctxt->myDoc);
note: When the parser reaches the end of the document, xmlValidateDocumentFinal is called. This walks the refs table which still contains pointers to freed IDREF attributes.
Scans the refs table. For each IDREF entry, calls xmlValidateCheckRefCallback which walks the ref list.
Walks the list of refs for each IDREF name.
Calls xmlValidateRef for each ref in the list.
Checks if the attribute pointer is NULL. In the vulnerable version, the ref->attr pointer is NOT NULL because xmlTextReaderRemoveRef was never called.
Dereferences the stale pointer to the freed attribute. This is the use-after-free.
Accesses freed memory. With XML_PARSE_NODICT, the attribute memory has been freed, so this reads freed heap memory.
Further dereferences the freed attribute's parent pointer, causing a heap-use-after-free read.
Compares the freed attribute's name with the IDREF name. This reads freed memory.
Accesses the children pointer of the freed attribute.
Dereferences the freed attribute's children to compare content with the IDREF name. This is the final use-after-free read that ASAN detects.
Frees the reader. The use-after-free has already been triggered during xmlValidateDocumentFinal.
Cleans up fuzzer data structures.
Returns from the fuzzer. The heap-use-after-free in xmlValidateRef has been triggered.
